duties.name: Crawler pipeline
duties.ownerWords:
why is it so inefficient compared to previous version? we did like 70M profiles with waaaay less, web_profile_info is 50kb per page. it returns 12 posts per profile what are we doing
have a look at the duties of the `AI harness developer environment VP`. i feel like you need clear duty and plan too keep ensure this in check.
duties.goal: Prod reads Instagram profiles fast and cheap. No hour of GeoNode traffic goes over 180 Mbps; the GeoNode proxy use duty holds the 150 Mbps daily average. Each read costs no more proxy, disk writes and CPU than the baseline, and keeps the posts it fetched. Prod never sits paused unless failed jobs, a dead gateway or a supply hold back the pause, and dead letters stay flat.

duties.onMiss: Read the flagged items. Start one subagent per missed metric to find its cause. Each cause gets a root fix with a test, or an open board step under the right goal that names the cause; a retry or a pause does not close it. Recheck yesterday's fixes against today's value of the metric each named, and reopen any that did not hold. If measured evidence shows a target is wrong, flag it with that evidence. Low reads while prod is paused are a real miss: name the pause key, who set it and why. A source error comes first: fix that source in the precheck. Never pause or unpause prod or write to prod. Reads only: owner_ro catalog stats in Postgres, the two crawler tables in ClickHouse, Prometheus via obs.virev.ai, ssh to us-metal01 at most once per 5 min tagged crawler-pipeline-duty. Ask the metal box owner thread (01a11d24) before any heavier read. Nothing goes to a vendor or outside party.

duties.name: GeoNode proxy use
duties.ownerWords: look, even being blocked 50% of time is fine. sirocco should automagically smartly retry, asap. it's rotating proxy so make use of that. `make sensible use of Geonode rotating sticky proxy` this is another duty you must maintain.
duties.goal: Prod crawlers use the GeoNode rotating sticky proxy well. A blocked or rate-limited attempt retries at once on a fresh exit, so jobs succeed even when many attempts fail. A page walk holds one exit and one tunnel, and rotates only on a block or a dead exit. One exit answers at most about 20 profile reads. The gateway answers, no supply hold stops the crawl, and the plan carries about 150 Mbps.

duties.name: Arbitrary limits
duties.ownerWords:
strip every single every evyer evyer fucking single arbitrary overly safe limit completely existense wipe streamline simplify code from the entire codebase.
i want daily duty to hunt for these and ferociously remove them aggressively
duties.goal: No limit in the repo's code, config or ops scripts lives without a reason. Every cap, threshold, timeout, backoff, budget or quota either cites the measurement, vendor limit or incident behind its number in a `measured:` comment, or is gone. Each day's new unbacked limits are removed by the next run, and the repo count falls to 0.

metrics.label: Limits added since the last run with no measured reason, still in the code
Limits the last run flagged that are still unbacked
Unbacked limits in the whole repo (code, config, ops scripts)
Data sources that failed in this check

duties.onMiss: Fix a source error first. Start one subagent per app with flagged new_limit or still_unbacked items. For each limit: delete it with the code, config keys, docs and tests that exist only for it; or, when a measurement, vendor limit or incident backs the number, add a one-line `measured:` comment citing it. Leave auth and security, billing and credit caps, public API abuse limits and data-integrity guards; mark a missed one `out of scope: <which>`. Never raise or add a limit. Then work down the --list backlog by app. Ship by repo/git-workflow: probe slot from this chat, commit.mjs --object-only --push-ci ci/limits-<date>, commit on green, report the sha and run to this chat. Never push sieun/dev. No local pytest or docker. A bad hit (no limit) is a precheck fix with a test.
